prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1098; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the left lane when the front of the vehicle struck the rear of Driver 2's vehicle at low speed while Driver 2 was slowing for a stopped vehicle ahead. Both drivers were stopped in the roadway when officers arrived. Driver 1 reported pain in the right shoulder and stated that the seat belt tightened sharply on impact, a account consistent with the force and direction of the collision. Driver 2 described the events in the same sequence, and two bystanders who had been waiting at the adjacent intersection gave statements that matched both accounts. Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the front bumper and hood of Driver 1's vehicle and the rear bumper of Driver 2's vehicle, which is consistent with the impact described. Officers confirmed that Driver 1 was seated behind the wheel at the time of the collision, and a Passenger in the rear seat was also identified and checked. Driver 1 stated there was no prior damage to the vehicle, and no earlier damage was observed during the inspection. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the insurance policy covering the vehicle.
